Vendored from: https://github.com/isar/libmdbx (mirror of the official libmdbx repository)
Tag: v0.13.9
Commit: 926e90ac9a13eb761afc85d37641e4acfa8ea998
License: Apache-2.0
Vendored: 2026-09-06

Layout: a minimal flat source set that `zig cc` compiles directly - no build
system of any kind is vendored (see "Build tool" below for how config.h/
version.c were produced, and why CMake itself isn't kept here). Assembled by
hand from a full source checkout, not upstream's own pre-packaged
amalgamation (that's only produced by their internal `make dist`, isn't
published as a downloadable release asset on the mirrors, and would still
need a build system to compile anyway):
  - mdbx.c is the original src/alloy.c (a unity-build file that #includes
    every other .c file) with its sibling .c/.h files copied flat alongside
    it instead of left in a src/ subdirectory.
  - version.c is hand-generated from src/version.c.in with this exact tag's
    version/commit/tree/timestamp substituted in.
  - config.h is CMake's generated output from src/config.h.in, produced once
    (see "Build tool" below) against the full source tree, then copied here.
  - mdbx.h is the only other file mdbx.c's own header search needs.
  - zig-shim/asm/cachectl.h is a stub for a header Zig's bundled glibc is
    missing (see build-linux-x64.sh for why).
  Nothing else lives here - no CMakeLists.txt, no CLI-tool sources
  (mdbx_chk.c etc.), no mdbx.c++/mdbx.h++, no ntdll.def. Those all existed
  only because a *previous* version of this vendoring used CMake, which
  required them to exist (even unused) to pass its own "is this the
  amalgamated distribution?" file-existence check. Once CMake was dropped
  from the day-to-day build path (see below), so was everything that existed
  solely to satisfy it - confirmed by rebuilding both platforms clean after
  removing them.

Two deliberate patches on top of the unmodified upstream content, both
required purely by this flat relocation / by a newer-than-upstream-tested
compiler, not logic changes:
  - essentials.h / preface.h: `#include "../mdbx.h"` -> `#include "mdbx.h"`
    (was relative to the old src/ subdirectory; mdbx.h is now a flat sibling).
  - gc-get.c: MDBX_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_AVX512BW's target string gained `,evex512`
    - newer LLVM/Clang (e.g. the one bundled with Zig, used for the actual
      builds - see below) splits `evex512` out from `avx512bw` as a distinct
      required feature for full ZMM register support; older/mainstream
      compilers don't need this.

Everything else from a full source checkout (test/, cmake/, docs/, example/,
packages/, conanfile.py, VERSION.json - the last was only a CMake input, not
needed once CMake itself isn't part of the build path) is simply not present
here - matching upstream's own "amalgamated: not for testing libmdbx itself"
distribution philosophy, just taken further since Zig needs even less than
CMake did.

## Build tool: one `build.zig`, four targets, callable from any host OS

`build.zig` builds `mdbx.dll` (x86_64-windows-gnu), `libmdbx.so`
(x86_64-linux-gnu), and `libmdbx.dylib` for both `x86_64-macos` and
`aarch64-macos` in a single `zig build` invocation - not hand-maintained
per-OS scripts. This is deliberate, not a convenience shortcut: rebuilding
any or all of these needs nothing but Zig (https://ziglang.org, tested
with 0.16.0) on PATH - no Visual Studio, no Xcode, no CMake, no
platform-specific toolchain at all, run from *any* host OS. CMake is only
needed once per vendored version bump, to (re)generate `config.h`/`version.c`
from the `.in` templates if they've changed upstream - not for routine
rebuilds (CMake itself isn't kept in this vendored tree at all; see above).
Every target gets `-DMDBX_HAVE_BUILTIN_CPU_SUPPORTS=0` (a real
`__builtin_cpu_supports` codegen/linking rough edge in Zig's bundled LLVM for
shared-library targets; trades one optional SIMD fast path for build
reliability, correctness unaffected) so all platforms behave identically
rather than silently diverging. The macOS targets needed no source patches or
extra linked frameworks beyond libc (`link_libc = true` already pulls in
libSystem, which is all libmdbx's Darwin code path needs) - unlike Windows,
which needs `ntdll` linked explicitly.

**Cross-verified all four host×target combinations, 2026-09-06**: built and
tested from both a Windows host and a Linux host (WSL2, once its networking
was fixed - see the project's session notes), producing both the Windows and
Linux binary from each. Three of the four were verified with a real
`dotnet test` run against the actual built binary (not just a successful
compile): Windows-host→Windows-binary, Linux-host→Windows-binary, and
Linux-host→Linux-binary all pass the same 5 tests in `RhinoDB.Test.Native`.
The fourth (Windows-host→Linux-binary) is verified structurally (all 14
required functions present in the ELF `.dynsym` table) since this sandbox
can't execute a Linux binary directly - but it's produced by the exact same
`zig build` invocation and flags as the three that were behaviorally proven,
so there's no reason to expect it to differ.

**Re-verified after the install-path fix, same day**: the two-vs-three `../`
bug above (fixed the same day, before this re-verification) meant the
original cross-verification pass was against binaries that had been manually
copied to the correct location for testing, not binaries `zig build` itself
had placed there. Re-ran Linux-host→Windows-binary and Linux-host→Linux-binary
end to end against the corrected `build.zig` (fresh WSL2 copy, `dotnet` SDK
reinstalled there since `/tmp`-adjacent state doesn't persist between
sessions) - both still pass all 5 `RhinoDB.Test.Native` tests, this time with
`zig build`'s own output consumed directly, no manual copy step involved.

**macOS targets added 2026-09-06, structurally verified only**: `osx-x64` and
`osx-arm64` both compile cleanly and produce valid 64-bit Mach-O shared
libraries (magic `0xfeedfacf`, cputype `x86_64`/`arm64` confirmed by
inspecting the header bytes directly). Unlike Linux, there's no equivalent to
the WSL2 trick available here to actually execute a Darwin binary from this
Windows sandbox, so `dotnet test` has not been run against either - that
needs a real Mac (or macOS CI runner) the first time someone builds a
`PersistentTable` against these. Same reasoning as the Windows-built Linux
binary above for why this isn't treated as a high-risk gap: identical source,
identical flags, identical build tool as the targets that were behaviorally
proven.

**Development workflow**: `mdbx.dll`/`libmdbx.so` are committed to git - a
normal RhinoDB build/clone/`dotnet test` never touches Zig, CMake, or the
vendored C source at all, exactly like consuming any other native-backed
NuGet package. `zig build` only gets run when the vendored source itself
changes (a patch here, or re-vendoring a newer libmdbx release) - run it from
this directory, verify (`dotnet test src/RhinoDB.Test.Native`), commit the
regenerated binaries alongside the source change. `.zig-cache/`/`zig-out/`
(this directory's build artifacts, distinct from the actual output which goes
straight to `../../../runtimes/{rid}/native/`) are gitignored.

**Install-path gotcha, found and fixed 2026-09-06**: `build.zig`'s
`InstallDir.custom` is resolved relative to the install prefix (`zig-out/`,
which lives inside this directory), not relative to `build.zig`'s own
directory - so reaching `RhinoDB.Native/runtimes/{rid}/native/` needs three
`../` segments (zig-out -> libmdbx -> vendor -> RhinoDB.Native), not two. The
original two-`../` version silently placed both binaries one level too
shallow, at `vendor/runtimes/...` - a real path, so the build "succeeded" and
the file "existed", just in the wrong place, which looked from the outside
like the file mysteriously vanishing when checked from the *intended* path
in a separate shell invocation. No antivirus or file-sync interference was
involved, despite that being the leading hypothesis for a while - worth
remembering if this ever needs debugging again.

Do not hand-edit anything here except by re-vendoring from a newer upstream
tag through this same process (or updating VERSION.json/version.c to match).
